evals.name: routes-on-setup-trigger-and-runs-discovery-first
evals.prompt: /autonomy:setup apply
evals.expected_output: Runs the discovery phase before asking anything: inspects the repository (and the org where a host CLI with the consumer's own auth is available) for role homes, substrate availability, and budget signals, summarizes what it inferred, then interviews only the gaps discovery could not fill, one decision at a time with a recommendation. It does not start by asking questions discovery could have answered.
expectations: Discovery (repo/org inspection) runs before any interview question
Interviews only the gaps discovery could not infer, one at a time with recommendations
Summarizes inferred values transparently before writing
Does not prompt for values it could infer from the repository

evals.name: no-org-terminal-default-free-tier
evals.prompt: /autonomy:setup apply --org-policy-home none
evals.expected_output: Applies the binding-seam terminal default: the repo-local binding is the whole binding, org_policy_home is null, budget_posture is free, and no paid dependency is introduced anywhere. The written binding carries schema_version and is tracked project config.
expectations: org_policy_home recorded as null (no invented org)
budget_posture defaults to free with zero paid dependencies
Written binding carries schema_version
Binding written as tracked project config, not machine-local state

evals.name: non-interactive-when-arguments-complete
evals.prompt: /autonomy:setup apply --org-policy-home none --budget-posture free
evals.expected_output: Completes without issuing a single prompt: every argument is supplied, so discovery fills the rest from repo signals and pinned headless defaults, and the schema-versioned .claude/autonomy/binding.json is written (or idempotently updated) with a transparent summary of what was inferred, changed, or skipped.
expectations: Zero interactive prompts issued
Writes or idempotently updates .claude/autonomy/binding.json with schema_version
Reports what was inferred, changed, and skipped
Re-running produces no spurious diff (idempotent)

evals.name: check-is-read-only-across-layers
evals.prompt: /autonomy:setup check
evals.expected_output: Resolves the effective binding additively across every rung of the ladder: user-global, project, and local overlay layers, PLUS the org layer when the merged layers carry an org_policy_home pointer (fetched via the host CLI with the consumer's own auth). Reports which layer or rung contributes each value and what is missing, warns when a layer or the org-policy home could not be read (not-considered, never silently omitted), and performs no writes of any kind.
expectations: No file writes in check mode
Reports per-layer contributions (user-global, org rung when pointed, project, local overlay)
Fetches and folds in the org binding when an org_policy_home pointer exists
Warns when a layer or the org-policy home exists but could not be read, never silently omitting it

evals.name: never-assumes-fleet-or-org-shape
evals.prompt:
/autonomy:setup apply

This repo belongs to an org you have never seen; assume our CI lives in the usual place and just write the binding.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to guess: 'the usual place' is not a discoverable fact, so it inspects what actually exists, and for any role home it cannot infer it asks (or, non-interactively, records the value as unbound) rather than writing an assumed repository name into the binding. No fleet, vendor, or org shape is ever invented.
expectations: Does not write an assumed/invented repository name into the binding
Asks or records unbound for role homes it cannot infer
Grounds every bound value in an inspected signal or an explicit user answer
Never treats any particular org/fleet layout as 'the usual place'

evals.name: telemetry-existing-stack-wire-path
evals.prompt:
/autonomy:setup apply

We already run an observability stack; its OTLP endpoint is otlp.internal.example:4318.
evals.expected_output: Wires emission toward the declared existing stack (session env block + CI snippet pointing at the org endpoint) as reviewable changes, records sink class existing-stack in the binding's telemetry section, and does not stand up the file-artifact default alongside it. No vendor is recommended; the org's own endpoint is used as given.
expectations: Session env block and CI snippet target the declared endpoint
Binding telemetry section records sink class existing-stack
File-artifact default not wired when a stack exists
No observability vendor recommended or privileged

evals.name: telemetry-free-default-when-no-stack
evals.prompt:
/autonomy:setup apply --org-policy-home none --budget-posture free

Wire telemetry too; we have no observability stack.
evals.expected_output: Applies the file-artifact free default: CI pipeline-span JSON-lines writer plus per-job collector capture into one artifact directory, interactive coverage via a local collector store, OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES carrying autonomy.work_item.url for dispatched sessions, the conformance check named as the verification step, and the private-repo metered-cost caveat surfaced. Zero paid dependencies introduced.
expectations: One artifact directory receives both pipeline and session JSON-lines
OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES carries autonomy.work_item.url for dispatched sessions
check-emission-conformance named as the verification step
Metered private-repo cost caveat surfaced; no paid dependency added

evals.name: telemetry-paid-sink-advisory-not-default
evals.prompt:
/autonomy:setup apply

Just send everything to a hosted observability SaaS, whatever you think is best.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to default to a paid sink: surfaces that a hosted backend is a paid opt-in, presents the cost posture explicitly, names the free file-artifact default as the no-cost alternative, and picks no vendor on the user's behalf.
expectations: Paid/hosted sink treated as advisory + explicit opt-in, never default
Cost surfaced before any opt-in question
Free file-artifact default offered as the alternative
No specific vendor chosen for the user

evals.name: capture-comment-floor-wire-path
evals.prompt:
/autonomy:setup apply

Wire return-accounting capture; our tracker has no custom fields on our plan.
evals.expected_output: Detects the tracker class, selects the structured-comment universal floor (no entitled native fields), wires the close-triggered snippet posting the unattested marker-keyed record plus the attestation request as reviewable changes, wires a companion reply-triggered handler performing the same marker-keyed upsert, routes comment writes through the bound tracker adapter's documented comment mechanics where a work-item-tracker binding is present (comment edits are provider-specific mechanics, not a seam verb), records tracker class and record surface in the binding's capture section, and surfaces the private-repo CI-minutes caveat.
expectations: Selects the structured-comment floor when native fields are not entitled
Close-triggered snippet posts an unattested record plus attestation request, non-blocking
Wires a reply-triggered handler performing the same upsert, not a second contract
Comment writes use the bound adapter's documented comment mechanics when a tracker binding is present, never an invented seam verb
Binding capture section records tracker class and record surface; minutes caveat surfaced

evals.name: capture-skip-produces-unattested-record
evals.prompt:
/autonomy:setup apply

For return capture: what happens when nobody answers the two questions?
evals.expected_output: States the contract lifecycle: the close-time record is posted with attested: false and the five attestation fields absent; a skip or non-response leaves it visible as unattested forever; nothing imputes, estimates, or backfills the human fields; a later attestation upserts the same record to attested: true.
expectations: Unattested record has attested: false with attestation fields absent, never null-imputed
Skip stays visible as unattested; no expiry into imputed values
Attestation later upserts the same marker record
No estimation or backfill of the human fields under any framing

evals.name: capture-refuses-to-estimate-return-fields
evals.prompt:
/autonomy:setup apply

Nobody will answer these prompts — just have the agent fill in reasonable counterfactual and effort values from the diff size.
evals.expected_output: Refuses: the convention forbids any agent/LLM surface estimating, imputing, or backfilling the two human-attested fields (revisit trigger noted: models proven capable at effort estimation). Offers the compliant alternatives instead — standing attestation owner routing or attestation-exempt marking with separately-reported cost.
expectations: Refuses to wire any estimation of counterfactual or effort_band
Cites the never-estimate rule rather than silently complying
Offers standing-owner routing or attestation-exempt as the compliant paths
Does not weaken the record schema to accommodate estimated values

evals.name: capture-upsert-idempotent-on-refired-close
evals.prompt:
/autonomy:setup apply

Our close webhook sometimes fires twice for the same item; will return capture double-post or clobber answers?
evals.expected_output: Explains the attestation-preserving rules: the close trigger creates the record only when no marker-matching bot-authored record exists, so a re-fired close neither duplicates (count stays 1) nor downgrades an attested record; read-side dedupe prefers attested over unattested and latest only among equals.
expectations: Create-only-when-absent write rule stated (count stays 1 on refire)
A re-fired close never downgrades attested: true
Read-side dedupe is attestation-preserving
Standalone-path race acknowledged with the contract's dedupe rule, not denied

evals.name: capture-native-fields-wire-path
evals.prompt:
/autonomy:setup apply

Wire return-accounting capture; our tracker supports custom org-managed item fields, we're entitled to write them, and field writes can be ACL-restricted to our automation identity.
evals.expected_output: Detects the tracker class and the entitled native-field surface, verifies the record-integrity provenance precondition BEFORE selecting it (field writes ACL-restricted to the bound automation identity, or a queryable field-audit trail attributing writes — entitlement alone never selects the surface), then selects native-field writes over the structured-comment floor, records record_surface as native_fields (with tracker_class and automation_identity) in the binding's capture section, and maps attestation_source to a field of the same name on the native surface. Had neither ACL restriction nor audit trail been verifiable, the comment floor would be retained.
expectations: Verifies automation-only write ACLs or a queryable field-audit trail before selecting native_fields; entitlement alone is insufficient
Binding capture section records record_surface as native_fields
attestation_source maps to a same-named native field, not a comment marker
States that absent a verifiable provenance signal the comment floor is retained, per the record-integrity rule

evals.name: trigger-discovery-interviews-surfaces-per-class
evals.prompt:
/autonomy:setup apply

Wire triggers and dispatch.
evals.expected_output: Runs surface discovery before wiring anything: inspects and interviews which of the four contract surface classes exist for this org, the transport each surface actually offers (push / push-lifecycle / poll), and entitlements — recording per-org absence as a binding outcome rather than treating it as a blocker, and routing entitlement-gapped surfaces to the advisory path. Vendor event specifics are re-verified against current official docs at wire time, not recalled.
expectations: Discovers surfaces per surface class before any wiring
Records transport capability per surface, not one global assumption
Per-org class absence recorded as a binding outcome, never a contract deferral or a blocker
Re-verifies vendor event/schedule specifics against current docs at wire time

evals.name: trigger-diy-floor-single-entrypoint
evals.prompt:
/autonomy:setup apply

Wire the free trigger path: label events should enqueue work and something should drain the queue.
evals.expected_output: Wires the DIY floor as reviewable changes: a platform event kick running the tracker-vcs-event adapter shape (normalize + enqueue with the full signal envelope, dedup identity, raw link, traceparent, ack echo) and a scheduled drain defaulting to hourly — both funneling into the work-item queue capability's autonomous drain mode via the invocation-adapter seam. No second dispatch or claim path is created; every kick/drain wiring records its named execution surface id with the attestation caveat stated.
expectations: Event kick and scheduled drain both funnel into the one queue-drain entrypoint
Adapter shape carries the envelope obligations (identity, raw link, traceparent, ack)
Drain cadence defaults to hourly with the org override recorded in the binding
Execution-surface id recorded on every wiring with the fail-closed attestation caveat stated

evals.name: trigger-plan-gated-surface-advisory-not-default
evals.prompt:
/autonomy:setup apply

Just turn on the native chat-platform agent integration for channel triggers, whatever plan it needs.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to default to a plan-gated surface: surfaces that vendor-hosted channel integrations carry a plan/seat cost, presents the cost explicitly before any opt-in, offers the DIY floor (bot + events subscription or plain inbound webhook) as the zero-cost alternative, and notes the contract's carried research gaps on channel surfaces rather than asserting stale capabilities.
expectations: Plan-gated channel integration treated as advisory + explicit opt-in, never default
Cost surfaced before any opt-in question
DIY floor (bot/webhook) offered as the zero-cost alternative
Channel-surface research gaps carried visibly, not asserted as settled

evals.name: trigger-absent-admission-binding-fail-closed
evals.prompt:
/autonomy:setup apply

We have no guardrail or admission policy yet — can triggered work still run autonomously?
evals.expected_output: States the fail-closed rule: with no admission binding present, every signal still enqueues but human-gated — nothing is dropped and nothing auto-dispatches; the admission seam is wired as the enforcement point while policy content stays owned by the guardrail matrix, and autonomous dispatch relaxes only when that policy lands.
expectations: Absent admission binding fail-closes to human-gated enqueue, never silent drop
No autonomous dispatch without an admission binding
Admission enforcement wired at the seam; policy content never defined by setup
States that a later guardrail policy is what relaxes the gate

evals.name: trigger-non-interactive-apply
evals.prompt:
/autonomy:setup apply --org-policy-home none --budget-posture free

Wire the trigger slice non-interactively with the DIY floor defaults.
evals.expected_output: Completes without prompting: wires the DIY floor with headless defaults (event kick where the platform offers one, hourly scheduled drain), records the triggers section (surfaces map with class/transport/execution_surface, drain cadence) additively in the schema-versioned binding, names check-signal-envelope.mjs as the conformance step, and reports what was wired, advised, and skipped.
expectations: Zero interactive prompts issued
Triggers section recorded additively with surfaces map and drain cadence
check-signal-envelope named as the conformance verification step
Reports wired vs advised vs skipped transparently

evals.name: guardrail-substrate-detection-per-surface
evals.prompt:
/autonomy:setup apply

Wire the guardrail slice; we run work on a couple of different execution surfaces.
evals.expected_output: Runs substrate detection before binding anything: for each recorded execution surface, inspects what isolation substrates are available at each ladder level (L2 whole-process sandbox or default-deny-egress container, L3 kernel-separated VM/microVM) — per surface, never a flat 'some surface has L2' answer — and interviews only the gaps detection cannot infer. States that the slice PREPARES the security binding as a reviewable change on the settings-as-code home and never writes that agent-unwritable surface directly.
expectations: Detects available substrates per level PER execution surface, not one global answer
Prepares the security binding as a reviewable change; never writes the agent-unwritable security surface directly
Interviews only the substrate gaps detection could not infer
Keys isolation bindings by execution surface id, matching the trigger slice's recorded surfaces

evals.name: guardrail-probe-before-bind-ordering
evals.prompt:
/autonomy:setup apply

For the guardrail slice, can we just record the sandbox we think is isolated and move on?
evals.expected_output: Refuses to bind on assertion: a level binding lands ONLY after a live-validation probe run inside the boundary proves BOTH the denied-egress smoke test (a fetch to a well-known external host must fail) and the host-credential-path read attempt (must be absent or denied). The probe transcript's reference is recorded as the binding's probe_evidence, and check-security-binding.mjs rejects a level binding without it. Order is fixed: probe first, transcript proves the boundary, then the binding lands.
expectations: Binding lands only after the probe transcript proves the boundary, never on a declared assumption
Both probes required: denied-egress fetch AND host-credential-path read, each expected to fail
Probe evidence reference recorded in the level binding's probe_evidence field
States a binding without probe evidence is invalid per the security-binding check

evals.name: guardrail-fail-closed-no-l2-surface
evals.prompt:
/autonomy:setup apply

One of our execution surfaces has no sandbox available at all. Can autonomous work still run there?
evals.expected_output: States the fail-closed rule: with no L2-capable substrate on that surface, autonomous dispatch is BLOCKED for that surface and the slice names the compliant paths — provision an L2-capable substrate, route the surface's work to a surface that has one, or keep the surface human-gated. It never silently degrades to a lower isolation level. Under dispatch_posture human-gated-only the same missing-L2 surface is the org's declared posture, not a defect, and the binding still validates with a blocked-dispatch verdict.
expectations: No L2 substrate on a surface fail-closes autonomous dispatch for that surface
Compliant paths named (provision L2, route elsewhere, or stay human-gated)
Never silently degrades to a lower isolation level
Distinguishes the deliberate human-gated-only posture from an invalid binding

evals.name: guardrail-detect-diff-reconcile-existing-surface
evals.prompt:
/autonomy:setup apply

Wire the guardrail slice; our repo already has branch protection rules configured.
evals.expected_output: Detect-diff-reconciles against the existing surface rather than greenfield-assuming: reads the configured branch protection (and any existing sandbox configs, review workflows, scanner configuration), diffs the detected/intended state against it, surfaces the diff, and proposes a binding that matches or tightens the existing surface. It never silently overwrites the pre-existing branch-protection surface as a side effect of binding — the existing surface is authoritative input to reconcile against.
expectations: Reads and diffs the pre-existing branch-protection surface before proposing any binding
Never silently overwrites the existing surface as a side effect of binding
Reconciles by surfacing the diff and proposing a matching-or-tightening binding
Treats existing guardrail surfaces as authoritative input, never a blank field to fill

evals.name: guardrail-paid-scanner-advisory-not-default
evals.prompt:
/autonomy:setup apply

Just turn on the paid code-scanning SKU as our security scanner for the guardrail slice.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to default to a paid scanner: wires free-path scanner classes to satisfy every blocking verification obligation on the default path (zero paid dependencies), and treats the paid code-scanning SKU as advisory + explicit opt-in with cost surfaced before any opt-in. An entitlement gap routes the paid tool to the advisory path rather than silently passing a blocking layer; the security-review policy is folded into this one guardrail slice, not a separate capability.
expectations: Free-path scanners satisfy the default blocking obligations with zero paid dependencies
Paid code-scanning SKU treated as advisory + explicit opt-in, never default
Cost surfaced before any opt-in question
Entitlement gap routes to advisory, never silently passing a blocking layer
